statement.text: A group $G$ is called an orientable Poincar\'e duality group of dimension $n$ over a ring $R$ if it is of type $FP$ over $R$ and $H^i(G;RG)=0$ for $i\ne n$, while $H^n(G;RG)=R$ as an $RG$-module, where the action on $R$ is trivial. (Note that $G$ is not required to be finitely presented.) If $G$ is an orientable Poincar\'e duality group of dimension $n$ over all fields, is it an orientable Poincar\'e duality group over the integers?
